---
name: festival-app
description: Open files, directories and workitems in the Festival desktop app and arrange its tabs and panes with `camp app`. Use when the user says "open that in the app", "open it in Festival app", "show me that in Festival", asks to put something beside something else in the app, or names `camp app` or `camp-app`.
---

# Festival App

Drive the Festival desktop app from the terminal with `camp app`.
`camp app` and `camp-app` run the same commands.

This skill covers the workspace app: camps, quests, tabs, panes, files and
terminals. These commands do not control the Activity timeline.

## Check first

```bash
camp app status
```

If `camp app` is not a command, or status reports that the app is not
installed, tell the user and stop. Do not look for another way to open the
file.

`camp app open` launches a closed app on its own. Pass `--no-start` when you
must not launch it.

## Open what the user asked for

| The user wants to see | Command |
| --- | --- |
| One file | `camp app open PATH --focus target` |
| A folder, or several files you just wrote in one folder | `camp app open DIR --focus target` |
| A tracked workitem | `camp app open --workitem REF --focus target` |

A directory opens as a workitem. When you wrote several files in one
directory and the user says "open it", open the directory, not one of the
files.

Where it lands:

- `--new-pane` opens it in a new pane to the right.
- `--split left`, `--split right`, `--split up` or `--split down` chooses the
  side.
- `--new-tab` opens it in a new workspace tab.
- `--replace` replaces what an explicit `--pane` holds. It can end a running
  terminal in that pane, so use it only when the user asks.

Pass `--focus target` when the user wants to look at it now. Pass
`--focus preserve` when you are arranging things in the background.

Tell the user which pane it opened in. The command prints the pane ID.

## Arrange tabs and panes

```bash
camp app tab list
camp app tab new TITLE
camp app tab focus ID
camp app pane list
camp app pane split --direction right
camp app pane move PANE --below OTHER
camp app pane focus PANE
camp app quest open QUEST
```

`camp app tab close ID` and `camp app pane close ID` refuse with
`RESOURCE_BUSY` when the tab or pane holds something that would be lost, such
as a running terminal, a browser page or an unsent chat draft. Never pass
`--force` unless the user told you to close it.

`camp app quest open` needs a quest ID or slug when an agent runs it.
`camp quest list --json` lists them.

## Which workspace a command acts on

With no selectors, a command acts on the camp you are in, and `camp app open`
uses that camp's current default quest. Inside an app terminal, commands act on
that terminal's workspace instead; pass `--no-context` to ignore it. To act
somewhere else, pass `--camp`, `--quest`, `--tab` or `--pane`. Read the IDs
from a snapshot.

## Layouts with several steps

1. `camp app snapshot --scope camp --json` reads the layout and its
   `revision`. `--scope tab`, `--scope quest` and `--scope window` also work.
2. `camp app schema apply --json` describes the batch document.
3. `camp app apply --file PLAN --dry-run --json` checks the plan against the
   live layout and changes nothing.
4. `camp app apply --file PLAN --json` applies it.

Put the snapshot's `revision` in the plan's `baseRevision`, so
`camp app apply` refuses when the layout changed in between. `camp app apply`
takes its targets and revision only from the plan. For a single command, pass
`--if-revision` with that revision for the same check.

## When a command fails

Pass `--json` so a failure comes back as one result with an error code.

| Code | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` | Tell the user. Stop. |
| `APP_NOT_RUNNING` | Run `camp app start`, then retry once, unless you passed `--no-start` on purpose. |
| `APP_UNAVAILABLE` | The app did not answer or could not be launched. Retry once, then tell the user. |
| `NO_CAMP` | Run from inside a camp, or pass `--camp`. |
| `PATH_NOT_FOUND`, `PATH_OUTSIDE_CAMP` | Fix the path. It must be inside the camp. |
| `WORKITEM_NOT_FOUND` | Check the ref with `camp workitem`. |
| `TARGET_NOT_FOUND`, `STALE_CONTEXT`, `REVISION_CONFLICT` | Your IDs are out of date. Take a new snapshot. If the camp is not open in the app, `camp app start` opens it. If the message names the terminal origin, pass `--no-context`. |
| `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET` | Add a selector such as `--instance` or `--window`. If the message says several app launch descriptors match, tell the user. |
| `NO_QUEST` | Pass an open quest's ID or slug with `--quest`, or to `camp app quest open`. `camp quest list --json` lists them. If none is open, tell the user. |
| `RESOURCE_BUSY`, `REPLACE_REQUIRED` | The pane holds a terminal, chat or browser. Closing or replacing it can lose a running terminal, a browser page or an unsent draft. Ask the user before you pass `--force` to close it or `--replace` to open over it. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` | Camp is missing from PATH or too old for this command. Tell the user. Do not retry. |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | The change may have applied. Run `camp app operation show REQUEST_ID` before you retry. |
| `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | The app did not apply it. Retry once with a longer `--timeout`. |
| `INTERRUPTED` | The command was cancelled before the app applied it. Retry only if the user asks. |

REQUEST_ID is the result's `requestId`, or `error.details.recoverableRequestId`
when that is set. Human output prints it in the error. A `camp app apply` that
fails with outcome `partial` applied its earlier steps; inspect it the same way
before you retry.
